title: Pediatric Resuscitation — 2025 ERC Changes
sources: Critical Vector — 2025 Pediatric Resuscitation: What Actually Changed (verified vs the primary document + RCUK / DFTB summaries)
Djakow J, Turner NM, Skellett S, et al; ERC Paediatric Life Support Writing Group. Resuscitation 2025;215(Suppl 1):110767

changelog.change: Initial entry — the bedside-relevant changes from the 2021 to 2025 ERC Paediatric Life Support guideline. BLS technique is unchanged; the changes are in advanced care.

summary: Pediatric BLS technique is UNCHANGED from 2021. The changes are in advanced care: hard numeric airway limits, a raised adolescent fluid-bolus cap, ideal-body-weight drug dosing in high-BMI children, a new defibrillation energy ceiling, and adult-level specificity for septic shock and massive haemorrhage.

body.text: Use newborn life support (NLS) during a neonatal / maternity-unit stay and, out of hospital, up to 24 hours of life; after that, use paediatric BLS. BLS compression rate, ratio, and rescue-breathing recommendations are unchanged from 2021.
Airway — numbers where there used to be judgement

items: Consider apnoeic oxygenation or HFNC to avoid hypoxia during intubation.
Limit each intubation attempt to 30–60 s; re-ventilate immediately for desaturation or bradycardia.
Maximum of 4 intubation attempts, then pivot to oxygenation (face mask or SGA) and call anaesthetics / PICU.

Fluid bolus 10 mL/kg — now up to 500 mL in adolescents (≥ 14 y), in line with adult practice (raised from the previous 250 mL cap). Balanced crystalloid preferred (Plasma-Lyte 148 or Hartmann's / LR).
IV access: no more than 5 minutes attempting IV before placing an IO; give analgesia for IO placement unless comatose.
Competent providers should use POCUS to guide difficult IV placement — an explicit recommendation now.

Vasoactive first-line agents specified: noradrenaline first-line vasopressor; adrenaline first-line inotrope; milrinone first-line inodilator. Vasopressor vs inotrope choice is left to clinical judgement.

TBI: titrate fluids and vasoactives to MAP ≥ the 50th centile for age; 0.9% saline may be preferred over balanced crystalloid HERE to drive mild hypernatraemia for neuroprotection — a deliberate exception to the balanced-by-default rule.

body.text: Obesity dosing fix: use IDEAL body weight, not actual, for resuscitation drugs in high-BMI patients — most are hydrophilic and don't distribute into fat, so actual-weight dosing risks overdose (including exceeding adult maximums).

rows: 4 J/kg, not exceeding the adult max (120–200 J, device-dependent)
Escalate stepwise to a maximum of 8 J/kg
Use the energy that previously achieved ROSC — don't reset to the initial dose
Antero-lateral (less CPR interruption); avoid breast tissue in adolescents
Up to 3 stacked shocks at 4 J/kg with rhythm/pulse checks between; if refractory, adrenaline + amiodarone AFTER 5 shocks, further amiodarone after 7

body.text: The peds drug-timing sequence differs from adult ALS (where amiodarone follows immediately after stacked shocks) — do NOT cross-apply the adult sequence to a pediatric arrest. If an arterial line is in place during CPR, target diastolic pressure > 25 mmHg (infants) or > 30 mmHg (children / adolescents) as a proxy for adequate coronary perfusion.
Special circumstances (now explicit, matching adult guidance)

items: Septic shock: blood cultures / PCR if feasible, broad-spectrum antibiotics within 1 hour. If refractory to fluids + first-line vasoactives (or adrenal insufficiency): hydrocortisone 1–2 mg/kg IV (max 100 mg).

Massive haemorrhage: TXA ASAP, within 3 h of injury — 15–20 mg/kg IV bolus (max 1 g), then 2 mg/kg/hr for ≥ 8 h (max 1 g / 8 h). Limit crystalloid to 20 mL/kg before moving to blood products. TBI or refractory shock: target MAP ≥ 50th centile for age.
